summary: We are testing whether replacing the iter-1 algorithm (strip construction + window 2-opt, score 55.4) with nearest-neighbor construction + spatial NN-list 2-opt (K=20) significantly improves the TSP-with-carrot-penalty score, and whether the construction heuristic choice matters independently of the optimization phase.
key_points: h-main: Full algorithm — greedy nearest-neighbor tour construction from city 0, then NN-list 2-opt using K=20 precomputed spatial neighbors (~1.7s), window 2-opt cleanup (~0.4s), and carrot step optimization. Predicted score: 70–80 (up from 55.4). Prior prototyping showed 76.3.

h-ablation: Same optimization phases (NN-list 2-opt K=20, window 2-opt, carrot) but with strip-based serpentine construction instead of NN construction. Predicted score: 65–75. Prior prototyping showed strip+NN-2opt at 71.2 vs NN+NN-2opt at 76.0, suggesting construction heuristic contributes ~5 points.

Confirmation criteria: h-main ≥ 70 confirms the spatial NN-list 2-opt mechanism works; h-main scoring ≥5 points above h-ablation confirms NN construction provides meaningful additional benefit. If h-ablation matches h-main within 3 points, construction choice is secondary and future iterations should focus on the optimization phase (e.g., Or-opt, 3-opt, LKH-style moves).

Risk factors to watch: NN precomputation could consume too much time on large N (up to 200K cities), leaving insufficient budget for 2-opt iterations. If score < 70, diagnostics point to checking time allocation and whether K=20 neighbors adequately cover true nearest neighbors in non-uniform point distributions.
Each arm runs ~45 seconds (20 test cases × 2.5s timeout + overhead). Total experiment wall time ~90 seconds for both arms.
